title: Expected distribution
view: Shared front-view base (visuals/distribution_bases/front): skeleton on the left, grey body on the right, patient's right on the image left; right-sided block.
teachingPoint: A saphenous (adductor canal) block numbs the medial leg and ankle and the medial border of the foot, with the periosteum of the medial tibia; the thigh is spared.
claims: Skin: infrapatellar branch (anteromedial knee below the patella), medial leg, medial ankle and medial foot border to the base of the big toe.

Not shaded: the thigh and the anterior knee above the patella (femoral cutaneous branches leave the femoral nerve above the adductor canal; the saphenous nerve is purely sensory and its branches come off in the canal and below).
Bone: saphenous periosteal patches on the medial upper tibia and the medial distal tibia with the malleolus (Lundblad et al. 2013). No femur, hip or knee-joint shading.
Right-sided block, patient's right on the image left (house laterality); one tone per nerve, key shown under the image in the app.

geometry.why: skeleton on the left, body on the right
